works.title: Design Patterns for Embedded Systems in C: An Embedded Software Engineering Toolkit
works.note: Names and teaches this route's hardware-access patterns (Hardware Adapter/Proxy, ISR, Polling, Debouncing) and the cyclic-executive/static-priority scheduling patterns.

works.title: Making Embedded Systems: Design Patterns for Great Software, 2nd ed.
works.note: Route entry point for bare-metal mechanisms: main-loop (super loop), interrupts vs polling, DMA, button debouncing, system tick.

works.title: Memfault Interrupt / Embedded Artistry canonical guides
works.note: Device Firmware Update Cookbook is the naming source and practical treatment of A/B firmware image update slots.

works.title: From Zero to main() series
works.note: 'How to Write a Bootloader from Scratch' names and walks the bootloader jump/handoff mechanism (vector relocation, stack swap, jump to app).

works.title: Linux Device Drivers, 3rd ed.
works.authors: Jonathan Corbet, Alessandro Rubini, Greg Kroah-Hartman
works.note: Canonical driver text: device-driver structure, top/bottom halves (deferred interrupt processing), DMA chapter, receive interrupt mitigation (coalescing/NAPI).

works.title: Real-Time Design Patterns; Doing Hard Time; Real-Time UML
works.note: Real-Time Design Patterns names Static/Dynamic Priority and Round Robin as scheduling patterns and treats the scheduler as a design element.

works.title: The Definitive Guide to ARM Cortex-M3 and Cortex-M4 Processors, 3rd ed.
works.note: Definitive treatment of the vector table/NVIC and of Cortex-M saturating (QADD/SSAT) arithmetic — upgrades saturation arithmetic beyond its Wikipedia naming.

works.title: ISO/IEC TR 18015:2006 — Technical Report on C++ Performance
works.note: The hardware-interface chapter defines the iohw.h standard hardware I/O interface — the naming source itself.

works.title: Dan Saks embedded.com columns on memory-mapped devices in C and C++
works.note: The canonical column series on memory-mapped register access idioms in C/C++ (volatile, placement, structs over registers).

works.title: C++ Hardware Register Access Redux
works.note: Naming source for typesafe register access via C++ templates; also a substantive treatment of memory-mapped access tradeoffs.

works.title: Patterns for Time-Triggered Embedded Systems
works.note: Names Super Loop and the time-triggered co-operative scheduler pattern language; cyclic-executive style schedulers throughout.

works.title: MicroC/OS-III: The Real-Time Kernel (also MicroC/OS-II; Embedded Systems Building Blocks)
works.note: Embedded Systems Building Blocks' fixed-point math chapter is the route's naming source; its timer-manager chapter teaches software timers.

works.title: Mastering the FreeRTOS Real-Time Kernel
works.note: Official kernel book: software timers, idle task hook, tickless idle, the tick interrupt, deferred interrupt processing, and the scheduler as taught mechanisms.

works.title: Hard Real-Time Computing Systems: Predictable Scheduling Algorithms and Applications, 4th ed.
works.note: The real-time scheduling theory text: cyclic executives, fixed-priority (RM) and dynamic-priority (EDF) scheduling, round robin, scheduler design.

works.title: Scheduling Algorithms for Multiprogramming in a Hard-Real-Time Environment
works.authors: C. L. Liu, James W. Layland
works.note: The founding paper: rate-monotonic (static priority) and EDF (dynamic priority) scheduling with utilization bounds.

works.title: Patterns for Fault Tolerant Software
works.note: Names the Deferrable Work pattern (shed/postpone non-critical work under overload).

works.title: Release It! Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software, 2nd ed.
works.note: Names the Governor stability pattern (slow down automated actions to human-supervisable rates).

works.title: Embedded C Coding Standard (BARR-C:2018)
works.note: Codifies ISR coding rules (naming, volatile discipline, keep-short constraints) — the coding-standard-grade treatment of the ISR element.

works.title: Modern C (3rd ed., C23)
works.note: The C23-era teaching text for checked integer arithmetic (<stdckdint.h> ckd_add/ckd_sub/ckd_mul) alongside the standard itself.

works.title: Hashed and Hierarchical Timing Wheels: Data Structures for the Efficient Implementation of a Timer Facility
works.venue: SOSP '87, Proceedings of the 11th ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, pp. 25-38
works.note: The naming paper for hashed/hierarchical timer wheels — O(1) start/stop/tick timer facilities; still the canonical reference for kernel and RTOS timer implementations. Verified via dblp record (dl.acm.org blocked this session).

works.title: Comparing Floating Point Numbers, 2012 Edition
works.note: The de facto canonical practitioner treatment of epsilon vs relative-epsilon vs ULP float comparison, including the near-zero failure modes.

works.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2024 — Information technology — Programming languages — C (C23)
works.note: C23 standardizes checked integer arithmetic via <stdckdint.h> (ckd_add/ckd_sub/ckd_mul). Adoption and identifier confirmed live on the WG14 committee site (open-std.org); iso.org blocked this session.

works.title: IEEE 1788-2015 — IEEE Standard for Interval Arithmetic
works.authors: IEEE Computer Society, Microprocessor Standards Committee
works.note: The standardization of interval arithmetic operations over IEEE 754 formats; confirmed live on standards.ieee.org (status inactive-reserved as of 2026, still the defining document).

works.title: Interval Analysis
works.unresolved: primary page not loadable this session; no ISBN cited
works.note: The founding monograph that named interval arithmetic/analysis; included as the naming source alongside the IEEE 1788 standard.

works.title: The Art of Computer Programming, Volume 2: Seminumerical Algorithms, 3rd ed.
works.note: Ch. 3 (Random Numbers) and sec. 4.3 (Multiple-Precision Arithmetic) are the canonical treatments of PRNGs and arbitrary-precision arithmetic. Verified on Knuth's Stanford TAOCP page.

works.title: What Every Computer Scientist Should Know About Floating-Point Arithmetic
works.note: The canonical floating-point survey: 'Relative Error and Ulps' section grounds ULP comparison; Theorem 8 states the Kahan Summation Formula. Verified via the authoritative Oracle/Sun reprint (ACM DL blocked this session).

works.title: Patterns of Enterprise Application Architecture
works.authors: Martin Fowler (with Rice, Foemmel, Hieatt, Mee, Stafford)
works.note: Names the Money base pattern (currency-aware amount object avoiding float rounding). Book page and Money catalog page loaded live on martinfowler.com.

works.title: Game Programming Patterns
works.venue: Genever Benning; free online at gameprogrammingpatterns.com
works.note: Names Update Method (ch. 10) and its Game Loop chapter (ch. 9) teaches fixed vs variable timestep tradeoffs. Contents page loaded live on the official site.

works.title: Fix Your Timestep!
works.note: The naming article for the fixed-timestep game/physics loop with accumulator and render interpolation; still the standard citation.

works.title: Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems
works.authors: Betsy Beyer, Chris Jones, Jennifer Petoff, Niall Richard Murphy (eds.)
works.note: Ch. 22 (Addressing Cascading Failures) names and teaches deadline propagation down RPC trees. Chapter loaded live on sre.google.

works.title: Scheduling Multithreaded Computations by Work Stealing
works.authors: Robert D. Blumofe, Charles E. Leiserson
works.note: The canonical work-stealing scheduler paper (Cilk lineage; basis of Java ForkJoinPool, TBB, Rayon). Verified via dblp record (ACM DL blocked this session).

works.title: Computer Networks, 6th ed.
works.authors: Andrew S. Tanenbaum, Nick Feamster, David J. Wetherall
works.note: The standard networking text: traffic shaping with leaky bucket and token bucket, and TTL/hop-limit semantics — the modern catalog-grade treatment for all three. Pearson catalog page loaded live.

works.title: RFC 1982: Serial Number Arithmetic
works.note: Defines wrap-around serial number comparison for 32-bit counters (DNS SOA serials; the pattern behind sequence-number comparison in protocols and embedded counters). Loaded live at rfc-editor.org.

works.title: RFC 791: Internet Protocol
works.note: Defines the Time to Live field — the naming source for TTL as a lifetime-bounding mechanism. Loaded live at rfc-editor.org.

works.title: AUTOSAR Classic Platform — Specification of Operating System (SWS OS)
works.unresolved: live page — autosar.org failed TLS verification this session; current release identifier not confirmed
works.note: The AUTOSAR OS specification defines schedule tables (statically configured expiry-point tables driving OSEK/AUTOSAR task activation) — the defining document for the element.

works.title: Meeting Real-Time Constraints Using 'Sandwich Delays'
works.authors: Michael J. Pont, Susan Kurian, Ricardo Bautista-Quintero
works.venue: Transactions on Pattern Languages of Programming I, LNCS 5770, Springer, pp. 94-102 (orig. EuroPLoP 2006)
works.note: The naming paper for the Sandwich Delay pattern (fixed-duration code sections to kill jitter in time-triggered systems). Springer chapter page loaded live.

works.title: A Guide to Debouncing
works.note: The empirical classic on switch bounce (measured bounce data for 18 switches) plus hardware and software debounce algorithms. Loaded live on the author's site.

works.title: Debouncing and Throttling Explained Through Examples
works.note: The standard UI-side treatment distinguishing debounce vs throttle (vs requestAnimationFrame) with interactive examples — anchors the throttle element and the event-side sense of debouncing.

works.title: Eliminating Receive Livelock in an Interrupt-driven Kernel
works.authors: Jeffrey C. Mogul, K. K. Ramakrishnan
works.venue: USENIX Annual Technical Conference 1996, pp. 99-112 (extended in ACM TOCS 15(3), 1997)
works.note: The canonical paper motivating interrupt mitigation/coalescing and hybrid interrupt-polling (NAPI lineage) — upgrades interrupt coalescing beyond its Wikipedia naming. Verified via research.google publication page.

works.title: PID Without a PhD
works.venue: Embedded Systems Programming, October 2000; maintained at wescottdesign.com
works.note: The embedded-practitioner classic on implementing and tuning software PID controllers in C without formal control theory. Loaded live on the author's site.

works.title: Feedback Systems: An Introduction for Scientists and Engineers, 2nd ed.
works.authors: Karl Johan Åström, Richard M. Murray
works.venue: Princeton University Press; full text maintained at fbswiki.org
works.note: The modern rigorous treatment of feedback control including a dedicated PID Control chapter; the freely maintained online edition is the current canonical text. Verified on the official book wiki.

gaps.why: Named only in vendor knowledge-base pages (Infineon write-only-register shadow-copy KB, Microchip PIC shadow registers) and ScienceDirect topic aggregations; no catalog-grade book/paper/standard treatment surfaced after a live search this session. Best upgrade candidates are MCU family reference manuals (official-doc grade, per-part rather than general); recorded as a gap rather than padded.

notes: Route r3 (embedded hardware-access, scheduling & time, numeric-precision): 50 of 51 elements covered by >=1 catalog-grade work; 1 gap (shadow-register, vendor-doc-only naming). Heavy membership reuse as expected: 19 memberships including douglasspatternsc/white/pont/freertosbook anchors, buttazzo+liulayland for scheduling theory (buttazzo was already in corpus, per seeds), yiu upgrading saturation arithmetic, gustedt pairing with the new C23 standard for checked arithmetic. 22 new works, 20 verified live (dblp used for the two ACM-DL-blocked papers timingwheels and blumofeleiserson; WG14 committee site for ISO/IEC 9899:2024 since iso.org 403s; Oracle authoritative reprint for Goldberg 1991). 2 unverified: mooreinterval (1966 monograph, no loadable primary page) and autosaros (autosar.org TLS failure). Economy choices: Tanenbaum Computer Networks 6e covers leaky-bucket + token-bucket + TTL in one node; Turner 1986 (leaky bucket naming) and Grand's Patterns in Java (Scheduler naming) omitted as buttazzo/douglassrtcorpus/freertosbook and tanenbaumcn cover those elements at better grade; ST AN2594 / FTL seeds rejected — no flash/EEPROM element in this route. Verified/unverified counts refer to new works only; memberships reuse corpus citations per the merge discipline.
